newsitem.title: USA: Pacificorp sees Q1 below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Pacificorp sees Q1 below forecasts.

text.p: PacifiCorp said it expects ts first quarter 1997 earnings to be below securities analysts' expectations and below first quarter 1996 results.
It said it expects that quarterly earnings could fall short of expectations by about 10 percent.

The shortfall is primarily due to higher power costs attributable to its Hermiston generating plant and reduced industrial revenues at its domestic electric operations. In its third quarter earnings release, the company said it expected the Hermiston plant would reduce operating income by about $30 million on an annualized basis.
According to First Call, the consensus estimate for the first quarter was $0.43 a share versus $0.42 a share.
PacifiCorp said its 1997 revenues will also be negatively impacted by about $9 million due to a rate reduction in its Utah jurisdiction, which went into effect April 15.

PacifiCorp President and Chief Executive Officer Fred Buckman said, "The company is examining various actions to improve 1997 earnings and believes it is too early to draw a conclusion about the implication of the first quarter shortfall on the full year."
PacifiCorp expects to report earnings the week of April 21.
